lesson_title: The Machine That Took 10 Jobs and Made 1 200 Shirts
hook_text: A new machine arrived at a Durban factory. Ten jobs disappeared, and output more than doubled. Here is what happened next.
clip_script: Before: 50 workers, scissors and old machines, 500 shirts a day. Then a computer-controlled cutter and new sewing machines. After: 40 workers, 1 200 shirts a day. That is technology raising productivity, and the factory going from labour-intensive to capital-intensive. Cheaper, better shirts win a big contract. But ten hand-cutters lost their jobs. Some were retrained as machinists. New jobs appeared: a machine technician and a computer designer. Technology takes some jobs, creates others and changes the rest. The people who win are the ones with skills: maths, reading, digital, problem-solving.
visual_style: A whiteboard factory floor shifting from rows of workers with scissors to a computer cutter, with job icons fading out and new ones appearing.
pacing: A quick before-and-after, a pause on the lost jobs, then new opportunities.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and list one skill you will start building for the jobs of the future.
